dataQualityNotes: Veterinary Public Health section reports activity for week ending 02 September 2026 within the Week 36 report ending 04 September 2026.
Suspected anthrax submissions are retained as suspected; no case count or location was stated in the source.
Absence of reported disease is not interpreted as absence of disease.

observations.title: Foot-and-mouth disease update
observations.summary: FMD cases were reported in Insiza, Mwenezi, Bubi and Lupane, all already in vaccination zones because of proximity to buffalo properties. Dry-season congregation at centralised watering points and illegal cattle movements linked to speculative marketing intermediaries were identified as challenges to control.

observations.title: Ticks and tick-borne diseases update
observations.summary: Tick-borne disease burden remained unusually high for the time of year and significantly above previous years. Dipping chemical supply was stable, although Treasury settlement of outstanding payments remained under negotiation. Fortnightly dipping continued in most areas; water-constrained dip tanks used pour-on treatments.

observations.title: Tsetse surveillance and control
observations.summary: Tsetse surveillance covered about 85 km² at seven trapping sites. Tsetse were also intercepted on vehicles at Marongora Gate arriving from Mana Pools and Chirundu. Insecticide-treated target deployment in Nyaminyami did not occur because 3-n-propyl phenol deliveries were suspended over unpaid debt; cumulative target coverage was only 602 km² of the planned 3,700 km².
observations.oneHealthRelevance: Directly relevant to integrated animal-human-vector surveillance because the same Makuti focus has recorded human r-HAT and tsetse circulation.

observations.title: Animal African Trypanosomiasis surveillance
observations.summary: No Animal African Trypanosomiasis cases were detected among 465 bovine blood samples from Doma, Save, Makonde and Chipinge.

observations.title: Human African Trypanosomiasis surveillance
observations.summary: No human African trypanosomiasis cases were reported by 13 referral and diagnostic centres during the week. The 2026 cumulative total remained two r-HAT cases including one fatality; both originated from the Makuti sleeping-sickness focus.

observations.title: Veterinary laboratory diagnostic services
observations.summary: Nationwide laboratory testing received 426 samples across five diagnostic disciplines. Virology accounted for the majority. The report emphasised timely testing, reporting and field feedback for early detection and response.

observations.title: Suspected anthrax laboratory submissions
observations.summary: The report states that a few suspected anthrax cases were submitted during the week. It does not provide a count, location or confirmation status.

observations.title: Plant extract-based acaricide research
observations.summary: Four crude extracts from four plant species achieved 90% larval mortality in Larval Packet Tests. Formulation optimisation, effective-concentration work and metabolite profiling are continuing, with a preliminary in-vivo animal trial planned within four weeks.

observations.title: Mazowe Bull Centre liquid nitrogen plant
observations.summary: The liquid nitrogen plant was installed and had operated for one week under engineer supervision with promising preliminary performance. It supports semen production and Theileria Bolvac vaccine production, storage, distribution and administration. DVS is exploring cryogenic storage for surplus production.

observations.title: Veterinary field data and service digitalisation
observations.summary: DVS entered the final phase of livestock data digitalisation, with remaining staff training planned. The system is intended to capture livestock census, disease reports, livestock movements and slaughter data. Livestock permit applications have also been digitalised and are already in use.
Veterinary port health processed 242 import and two export consignments at ports of entry/exit. Illegal animal products were confiscated and destroyed by incineration.

Dairy services included milk-quality testing, dairy-farm inspections and training in clean milk production and dairy-herd management. Animal-welfare and good-manufacturing-practice training was also conducted at Mvuma Rural District Council.

source: Directorate of Veterinary Services Weekly Highlights, Week 36 ending 04 September 2026
